title: SE Critical Paths: Sell Deck Sketch
content:
Purpose:
Quick, skimmable slide set for SEs to run discovery and negotiate capacity/latency tradeoffs with engineering/platform buyers. Focus: identify the critical path (decision maker, SLOs, cost trigger, pilot success criteria), and provide short, repeatable scripts + one-page ROI logic that sellers can adapt on call.

Target audience:
- Platform engineers & infra architects at mid-market/enterprise
- SEs running pilot/onboarding conversations

Slide 1 — Title + Hook
- Title: "Critical Paths for Inference Pilots"
- Subtitle: "Turn a technical pilot into a committed Reserved Capacity conversation"
- Speaker note: 15s opener: "We help you make inference predictable — not just fast. Today I want to map the critical path for your team so we can make pilot success repeatable and avoid surprises on cost and latency."

Slide 2 — Two-minute decision map (visual)
- Top row: Stakeholders (Platform Eng, ML Eng, Security, Finance)
- Middle: Key signals (latency SLA, throughput spikes, data residency, budget guardrails)
- Bottom: Desired outcomes (pilot pass criteria, committed capacity, ongoing ops SLA)
- Speaker note: Walk through typical handoffs. Ask: "Who owns the 99th pct latency? Who signs budget for reserved capacity?"

Slide 3 — Conversation lanes & scripts (condensed)
- Lane A: Latency-first integration
  - Trigger question: "What p95/p99 targets matter to your UX?"
  - Quick script: "If p99 > X ms under X TPS, we recommend Reserved + locality routing. We can show a simulated canary and cost delta in 20 minutes."
- Lane B: Cost-constrained embedder
  - Trigger question: "What's your monthly token budget/shock tolerance?"
  - Script: "We can add KV prefix caching and mixed-quantization variants to reduce unit cost by Y% while meeting quality constraints. Pilot metric: tokens-per-session and quality delta < 2% on eval set."
- Lane C: Compliance/Private deployment
  - Trigger question: "Do you need VPC or on-prem? Any encryption/HSM requirements?"
  - Script: "Private deployment enables audit logs and key control — expected lead time 6–10 weeks. We can run a security checklist in one call."

Slide 4 — One-page economics (plug-and-play fields)
- Fields for SE to fill on call: average tokens/session, sessions/day, target p95 latency, current infra cost estimate
- Example calc (placeholder numbers):
  - Tokens/session: 800
  - Sessions/day: 10k (monthly ~300k)
  - Hosted per-token cost: $0.0003/token => monthly = $90
  - Dedicated reserve cost (baseline): $5k/month for predictability and lower per-token marginal
  - ROI trigger: if expected monthly tokens > 1M or sustained p99 > 800ms, reserved capacity breaks even in ~3 months when including ops cost savings and outage risk mitigation.
- Speaker note: emphasize how to tailor numbers quickly: use approximate scaling to show when to shift from hosted to reserved.

Slide 5 — Canary & fallback play (ops checklist)
- Simple canary run steps: traffic sample, stress test, KV cache warmup, monitor p50/p95/p99, compare quality on eval set
- Rollback triggers: p99 increase > 30% or error rate > 0.5% for 10 minutes
- Fallback options: route to previous model variant, reduce request size, enable batching off-peak
- Speaker note: translate to SE action items: "I'll provision a 1-hour canary and share a dashboard with p50/p95/p99 + cost burn rate."

Slide 6 — Objection scripts (compact)
- "We already have infra": "Great — can we run a 2-week side-by-side? We'll show cost and latency tradeoffs and a migration plan if it helps."
- "Cost is too high": "Let's model your tokens/day — I can show a 1-page ROI that includes ops savings and outage risk."
- "Security concerns": "We do private deployments and KMS integrations — what's on your checklist? We can map it to our controls in 15 minutes."

Slide 7 — Pilot success criteria template (copyable)
- Latency: p95 <= X ms under defined TPS
- Quality: automated eval score drop <= 1.5% vs baseline
- Cost: tokens/month < Y or cost delta <= Z% expected
- Operational: rollback plan, alerting on p99 spike, runbook owner assigned
- Acceptance: sign-off from Platform Eng + Finance

Appendix A — Quick surgery scripts (for SEs)
- Live demo script (4 minutes): 30s context, 90s architecture, 90s demo showing latency chart under load, 30s next step ask
- Pre-call ask email template: 3 bullet items (expected TPS, top 2 performance concerns, compliance needs)

Appendix B — Example call transcript snippets
- "We saw p99 of 2.1s in staging" -> SE reply: "Let's do a focused canary with 10% of production traffic plus KV warmup — most p99 issues are cache-warming related and are visible in the first 60 seconds."

Notes to self / TODO:
- Add real cost numbers from finance (Diego to share reserved capacity SKU) — TODO @Diego
- Build quick Google Sheet to automate ROI numbers (linked_artifacts points to sheet after created)
- Validate rollback triggers with SRE team (Lina)
- Shorten slide owner scripts to single-sentence bullets for speaker one-liners

Open questions:
- What's the standard contract length we pitch for customers landing from pilot to reserved? (contract team input)
- Are there regional SKUs we should call out for APAC customers? (pricing ops)

Intended velocity:
- Aim to ship V0 of slides for SE trial by 2025-03-10
- Iterate after 3 live pilot calls, then formalize into a 4-slide quick card for AEs
